newsitem.title: UK: Echo Bay keys expansion to $375 gold price.
newsitem.headline: Echo Bay keys expansion to $375 gold price.

text.p: Echo Bay Mines Ltd is looking for a gold price of $375 per ounce upon which to base go-ahead decisions for its portfolio of development projects, officials told Reuters.

"We are looking at $375 in the longer term for our feasibility studies' construction decisions. We think $375 will prevail longer term," president and chief executive officer Richard Kraus said on Monday.
He said gold -- which fixed at $343.60 on Monday -- had bottomed out around 3-1/2 year lows.

"We would generate cash flow at $330-$340 per ounce but we would not be adding to our income statement," Kraus said, adding that amortisation and depreciation costs at Echo Bay averaged about $100 per ounce of gold produced.
The company, which is the sixth largest gold miner in North America, produced 768,000 ounces of gold last year and 7.1 million ounces of silver.
It reported a loss of $177 million in 1996, of which $107 million was one-off payments. After $81 million in cash flow was generated, $163 million was invested into the business, Kraus said.
"We will not have these costs again," Kraus said, adding that 1997 was a year in which Echo Bay would "regenerate itself".
The company bought back its gold and silver hedges at a $350.00 gold price and made a cash profit of $63 million.
"We would put hedges back on at above $375 if we considered the market had good upside potential," Kraus said.
Echo Bay has traditionally centred its production on North America but had diversified across Central and South America and also had properties under study in the Philippines, West Africa and Russia.
The company used as a minimum size a project of one million recoverable ounces of gold capable of yielding 100,000 ounces per year.

Its portfolio of potential developments was "ramped up" during 1996 with an exploration budget of $64 million which will be trimmed to $31 million this year now that it has discarded some prospects, allowing developmental work to be more focused, Kraus said.

Two mines, Aquarius near Timmins, Ontario, and Paredones Amarillos near La Paz, Baja California Sur, Mexico, are being brought into production. Aquarius is 100 percent owned by Echo Bay and the Mexican project is a 60-40 joint venture with Viceroy Resource Corp of Vancouver.
The two new mines will add about 250,000 ounces to Echo Bay's annual production when they gear up from a late 1998 start-up to full production the following year.
Cash costs at the two mines were forecast at $220-$225 per ounce and total operating costs at about $320-$325. Echo Bay's current cash cost of gold production is around $245-$255.
Its expansion programme has been fashioned on the basis of developing a project "pipeline" involving joint ventures or partnerships, mainly with local companies.

A potentially major project is the 50-50 joint venture with Ashanti Gold Fields Co at Youga on the Burkina Faso-Ghana border where drilling to date has revealed an average of 1/3-1/2 ounce of gold per tonne and several metres of over an ounce.
"It is too early to say how big Youga could be. We will know in 1997," said Robert Wunder, senior vice president for project development.
Last year Echo Bay Mines absorbed $77 million to write off its Alaska-Juneau property, which Kraus said "was not economical enough."
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
